senses.definition: present participle and gerund of hiss

quotes.text: Our solid, shiny chairs, our immense, dingy sofas, our heavy mahogany tables and our cast-iron fenders, often bearing the initials of long-dead railway companies, likewise our plaster walls of chocolate and duck-egg green and our hissing gasoliers have their roots deep in our national history.
quotes.reference: 1941 August, C. Hamilton Ellis, “The English Station”, in Railway Magazine, page 357:

senses.definition: that produces or is accompanied with a hiss

quotes.text: At all times when kissing and such like things are begun, the woman should give a reply with a hissing sound.
quotes.reference: 1883, Richard F[rancis] Burton, transl. and editor, Karma Sutra:

quotes.text: The hissings and screamings of the vulgar against him as he moved forward on his stedfast course he heeded less than those of geese on a common.
quotes.reference: 1875, John Lothrop Motley, The Life and Death of John of Barneveld Advocate of Holland:
